meta.title: The Best LocalSend Alternative — Local Speed + a Link for Anyone
meta.description: Love LocalSend but need to reach people who aren't on your network? BIShare sends files instantly device-to-device like LocalSend, and adds browser link sharing, cloud storage and sync — free, end-to-end encrypted, on iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac and Linux.

hero.title: Everything you love about LocalSend — plus reach beyond your network
hero.body: LocalSend is a great open-source way to send files between devices on the same Wi-Fi. BIShare does that too — instant and end-to-end encrypted across every platform — and then goes further: a browser link for anyone who isn't nearby, plus cloud storage and sync.

why.title: Where LocalSend stops
why.body: LocalSend is built for one job and does it well: direct transfers between devices on the same network. But that's also its boundary — if the other person is in another city, on mobile data, or behind a different router, there's no way to reach them, and there's no cloud to keep your files in sync between your own devices.

how.title: How BIShare picks up where LocalSend leaves off

0.b: On the same Wi-Fi, BIShare sends device-to-device at local-network speed, end-to-end encrypted, across iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac and Linux — exactly the LocalSend use case, no cloud detour.

1.b: When the recipient isn't on your network, share a link or a short code they open in any browser — no app and no account on their end. This is the piece LocalSend doesn't have.

2.h: Cloud storage and sync when you want it
2.b: Folder sync across your own devices and rooms for group sharing — all optional, all end-to-end encrypted. Use it like LocalSend and ignore the cloud, or lean on it when you need continuity.

rows.r0: Instant local transfer across all platforms
rows.r2: Reach someone not on your network (link)
rows.r3: Recipient needs no app (opens in a browser)

0.q: Is BIShare open source like LocalSend?
0.a: LocalSend is fully open source; BIShare is free to use with an open, documented transfer protocol and end-to-end encryption. If open source is your only requirement, LocalSend is a great pick — if you also need link sharing and cloud sync, BIShare covers more ground.

1.q: Does BIShare work on the same network without the cloud, like LocalSend?
1.a: Yes. On the same Wi-Fi, transfers go straight device-to-device at local speed and never touch the cloud — the cloud features are entirely optional.

2.q: Can BIShare send to someone in a different location?
2.a: Yes — that's the main thing it adds over LocalSend. Share a link or short code and the recipient opens it in any browser, wherever they are, with no app or account.

3.a: iPhone, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and the web — the same broad platform coverage as LocalSend, plus a browser experience for recipients.

4.a: Yes — all of it. Sending and receiving are free, the recipient never needs an account, and links expire automatically. BIShare is open source (MIT) and has no paid tier.

cta.title: Keep the local speed. Lose the network boundary.
cta.body: Install BIShare free on every device. Instant on your network, a link for everyone else, end-to-end encrypted throughout.
